issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Animal.messageOnFeed(): The problem statement and UML explicitly specify messageOnFeed() as returning a String (see UML: "messageOnFeed():String" and the class-specific instructions that say messageOnFeed() should return literal strings like "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). In the solution repository, Animal.java declares the method as "public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed()" and the concrete classes (Seal, Pig) return FeedResponse instances. The solution also introduces a FeedResponse class. This creates a conflicting contract: students following the problem statement will implement messageOnFeed() to return String, while the solution uses a wrapper type, causing confusion and potential compilation/type errors or mismatches when Farm or tests expect a plain String message.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the design consistent. Preferred fix: change the solution artifacts to match the problem statement by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and update Seal, Pig, and Goat to return the message strings (e.g., "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"); remove or stop using FeedResponse. Update any Farm or test code that prints messageOnFeed() to work with String. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement, UML, template, and tests to document and require FeedResponse as the return type (including how to extract the message), but only do this if the exercise is intentionally teaching wrapper/result objects.
